children: Asian currencies will continue to tread water as a fresh U.S. tariff salvo rekindles trade uncertainty, Maybank analysts say. Fracturing trade relations are negative for the dollar and the DXY index has fallen since the tariffs were first brought to attention, they write. The Trump administration has proposed duties targeting 14 economies over excess manufacturing capacity. Vietnam faces the highest proposed rate, followed by India, and then China and Singapore. Maybank notes that product exemptions--particularly for semiconductors and pharmaceuticals--could cushion the impact on Taiwan, South Korea, Singapore and Malaysia. There is also scope for negotiations to yield lower potential rates. With hearings scheduled to start in late January, tariff-related uncertainty could persist well into 1Q 2027, Maybank says. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
